(By Sri.H.K.Ramamurthy, Adv.)
 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .45,00,000/- for the death of H.M.Babu S/o Late Munivenkatappa in a road traffic accident.

2.It is stated in the petition that on 15-09-2023 at about 7:15 p.m., the deceased, Babu, was riding a motorcycle bearing registration number KA-07-EE- 2303,behind Bethamangala Police Station on Kolar- Bethamangala Road, V. Kota, KGF Road Junction, KGF Taluk, Kolar District.

At that time,
the driver of a Mahindra Pickup LGV bearing registration number KA- 08-A-1927 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed, and swerved onto Kolar Road.
As a result, the offending vehicle collided with the deceased Babu, causing him to fall and sustain multiple injuries.
3. Babu was immediately taken to the Government Hospital, Robersonpet, KGF.
Despite prompt medical attention, he succumbed to his injuries on the way to the hospital.
After the post-mortem examination, the petitioner received the dead body and performed the last rites.
4. The petitioner is the mother of the deceased.
It is stated that prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 33 years, and working as a mason, earning Rs. 30,000 per month.
The petitioner, being dependent on the income of the deceased, suffered mental shock, agony, and loss of the primary breadwinner of the family due to his untimely death.

5. It is further stated that the petitioner incurred expenses of Rs. 1,00,000 towards transportation,
funeral, and associated rites.
The petitioner has asserted that the driver of the offending vehicle is solely responsible for causing the accident.
6. Accordingly, the petitioner has requested that compensation of Rs. 45,00,000, along with interest, be awarded by the respondent, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
7. n response to the petition notice, Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsels.
Respondent No. 2, however, has failed to file a formal written objection.
8. In the objection statement filed, Respondent No. 2 has admitted the existence and validity of the insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
It has, however, stated that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
9. The Respondent contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not hold a valid driving license and denied both the involvement of the vehicle and the manner in which the accident occurred.
Further, it denied any negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident.

sentences.text: On the other hand, Respondent No. 2 has alleged that the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding by the deceased on the motorcycle.
It was contended that the deceased did not possess a valid driving license and was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.
11. The Respondent also contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.

It denied the claimed income of the deceased, the relationship of the petitioner with the deceased, and the petitioner's dependency on the deceased, and therefore prayed for the dismissal of the petition.
12.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 15- 09-2023 at about 7.15 p.m., on Kolar - Bethamangala road, V.Kota road junction, K.G.F Taluk, Kolar District, H.M.Babu S/o.Munivenkatappa, son of petitioner No.1 and 2, sustained injuries in a road traffic accident,
while he was riding his two wheeler number KA-07-EE- 2303, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Pickup LGV vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 08-A-1927 and succumbed to the injuries on the spot?
2. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by Respondent No.1 and the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
if any, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
13. The father of deceased was examined as PW-1 and produced documents marked as Ex.P.1 to P.11.
However, PW1 passed away on 16-06-2025 during the pendency of the petition.
14. The Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 and 2.

The driver of offending vehicle is examined as RW-2 and DL extract is marked as Ex.R.3.
15.
I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

16. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Negative Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:

3 REASONS 17. ISSUE NO.1:-

The petitioner has stated that on 15-09-2023 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Babu was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No. KA- 07-EE-2303 behind Betamangala Police Station, on the Kolar-Betamangala Road, near V. Kota, KGF Road Junction, KGF Taluk, Kolar District.
At that time, the driver of the offending vehicle drove in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed, and swerved onto the Kolar Road.
As a result, the offending vehicle collided with the motorcycle of the deceased Babu, causing him to fall and sustain multiple grievous injuries.
The injured was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Robertsonpet, KGF, but despite prompt medical attention, he succumbed to his injuries on the way to the hospital.

18. To substantiate their claim, the father of the deceased was examined as PW-1, and he produced police documents marked as Exhibits P-1 to P-8, which include the FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar,
IMV Report, Inquest Report, and Post-Mortem Report, as well as the Charge Sheet.
19. On the other hand, the Respondent No. 2 - Insurance Company contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself.

It was argued that the deceased was riding the motorcycle rashly and negligently, without wearing a helmet, without holding a valid driving licence, and without observing the movement of other vehicles.

According to the respondent,
the deceased's own negligence caused him to lose control of the motorcycle, leading to the accident.

20. To disprove the petitioner's case, the official of the Insurance Company was examined as RW-1,
who reiterated the contents of the written statement.

The driver of the offending vehicle was examined as RW-2, and he deposed that on 15-09-2023 at about 7.15 a.m., while proceeding from Bangarpet to Chennai, one person who had consumed alcohol, was not wearing a helmet, and was riding the motorcycle negligently, dashed against his vehicle, and that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, not on his part.
21.
During cross-examination, the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No. 2 suggested to PW-1 that the deceased had consumed alcohol and was riding negligently without a helmet or valid licence.
However, PW-1 denied all such suggestions, and no material admissions favorable to the respondents were elicited.
Although RW-1 and RW-2 contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, they failed to produce any cogent or credible evidence to substantiate their claim.
There is no material on record to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased or that it was a self-accident.

22. The Learned Counsel for the Petitioner placed reliance upon the decision reported in 2024 ACJ 849 -- Kallappa Arjun Kolkar vs. Riyajaammad H Mulla and Another and 2024 ACJ 1872 - Sadath Ali Khan V NOOR Ahmed Sayeed and another wherein the Hon'ble high court of Karnataka.

sentences.text: held that although the motorcyclist did not possess a valid driving licence at the time of the accident, such non- possession of licence cannot, by itself, be construed as contributory negligence or as a proximate cause of the accident.

In that case, the Hon'ble Court apportioned negligence to the Yashodamma vs Nagaraja B S on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25726242/
4 extent of 25% on the motorcyclist and 75% on the van driver, emphasizing that absence of a licence is a statutory violation or an offence under the Motor Vehicles Act, but not sufficient in itself to establish negligence in causing the accident.
23.

Placing reliance on the said judgment, the petitioner contended that mere non-possession of a driving licence may constitute a legal offence, but it does not automatically imply negligence on the part of the deceased, nor can it be treated as a contributory factor in the occurrence of the accident.
The learned counsel further argued that the deceased motorcyclist was riding carefully and that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle's driver was the sole cause of the accident.
vehemently contended that the deceased was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident and did not possess a valid driving licence.
Therefore, according to this respondent, the petitioners are not entitled to any compensation.
Alternatively, it was argued that, if the Tribunal were to hold the petitioners entitled to compensation, contributory negligence should be attributed to the deceased.

25. In support of this contention, reliance was placed on the judgment in MFA No. 7074/2016 -- Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. v. Naresh Babu Y.N. and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that a person riding a motorcycle must wear protective headgear and possess a valid driving licence at the time of the accident, and that a person riding without a licence may not be entitled to claim compensation.
26.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having carefully considered the said decision and perused the material available on record, this Tribunal finds that the facts and circumstances of the present case are distinguishable.

Though the respondents have alleged that the deceased was not wearing a helmet, had consumed alcohol, and was riding without a valid driving licence, no documentary evidence has been produced to substantiate these allegations.

The record only contains the oral testimony of RW-1 and RW-2,
which remains uncorroborated.
27.

A careful scrutiny of the police documents, including the FIR, spot mahazar, inquest report, and charge sheet, reveals that nowhere is it mentioned that the deceased was either without a helmet or without a driving licence at the time of the accident.
Hence, the factual foundation necessary to apply the ratio laid down in Naresh Babu's case is absent in the present matter.

28. Accordingly, while this Tribunal accords due respect to the ruling cited by the respondent no 2,
it finds that the facts of that case are not squarely applicable to the present case.
The plea of contributory negligence, therefore, cannot be sustained merely on unproved allegations.

29. Upon evaluation of the entire oral and documentary evidence, including the testimony of PW-1 and the police records, it is evident that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same, and the charge sheet filed by the police further corroborates the negligence of the offending vehicle's driver.

sentences.text: It is also well settled that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation, and strict proof of negligence is not required; rather, the preponderance of probabilities is sufficient to establish liability.

In view of the above discussion and evidence, the Tribunal holds that the deceased Babu sustained fatal injuries in the road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle's driver.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
31. ISSUE NO.2:-
The respondent No.2 has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2 -insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent no 2 has failed to prove his contention.
The offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, hence fastening joint liability on the Respondent no 2- insurance company
Wherefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answer issue no.2 in the negative.
32. Issue No.3 :-Petitioner is the mother of the deceased.
In order to prove her relationship, PW-1 has produced the inquest report at EXP6, voter ID card and Aadhaar cards of the deceased and Petitioner, which are marked at Ex.P.9 and 10.
The details in the above records show that deceased Babu is the son of Petitioner.
Petitioner is considered as dependent upon the income of the deceased.

33. On perusal of records, it is found that Petitioner has produced the Voter ID card of deceased at Ex.P.9, which shows the date of birth of the deceased as 01-01-1990 and as such, age of the deceased is considered as 33 years at the time of accident and appropriate multiplier applicable is 16.
34.

It is stated that deceased Babu was working as a mason and earning Rs.30,000/- P.M. and he was the only bread earner of the family and contributing his entire earnings towards maintenance of the family.
35. To prove the income and avocation of the deceased, the Petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the deceased could be assessed at Rs.16,000/- Per Month.
36. As the age of the deceased was age below 40 years, 40% future prospects is to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the monthly income would be .22,400/-.

Since, deceased was bachelor,
50% of his income shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and then the annual income would come around .11,200 x 12 = .1,34,400/- and by applying 16 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be Rs.21,50,400/-
37.
CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioner is entitled .44,000/- under the head of filial consortium as the Petitioner has lost her son, who was support for her.

sentences.text: Loss to estate:
The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner has lost her son.
Hence, .20,000/- towards loss to estate.
39. Transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances, it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the transportation of dead body, funeral & other incidental expenses.

1 40. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioners under various headings is as follows :
 Nature of Compensation Amount  1. Loss of dependency . 21,50,400/-
 2. Loss of Consortium . 44,000/-
 3. Loss to estate . 20,000/-
 4. Transportation of dead body, . 16,500/-
 Funeral & obsequies  Expenses  Total . 22,30,900/-
41. Liability:
It is already held that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 and 2 being insurer and insured are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observations I answer Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
42. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .22,30,900/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of amount, 25% of amount shall be kept in FD in the name of Petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 2 years and remaining 75% with entire interest shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
